title: What Are the Wedding Traditions Worth Keeping?
audience: Couples in their 30s, affluent, interested in a destination wedding and other luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

URL change: the new post lives at /expert-advice/wedding-traditions. Recommend (do not do) a 301 redirect from the old URL to the new one at publish, and updating internal links that point to the old URL; list those in the run report and backlinks-todo. Nothing on the live site changes.

Origins of traditions are myth-prone: every origin or history claim needs a reputable source (encyclopaedias, museums, national libraries, academic or official heritage sources). Contested origins are written as 'often said' with the documented version, or left out. No invented etymology.

'Worth keeping' is our editorial judgement, framed as such: for each tradition say what it means, where it comes from (sourced), and how couples keep, adapt or skip it, especially at a destination wedding.
Inclusive and gender-neutral where the tradition allows; traditions that assume a bride and groom are described accurately, with modern adaptations offered, never mocking.
Destination angle: local traditions couples can borrow at popular destinations, linking our existing tradition pages (Italy, Indian, Muslim, Arab, Lebanese, vows) rather than repeating them.
Fast mode: 02, 03 and 04 in parallel after the brief; 5 SERP cities; editor and readers in parallel; one combined final pass.

Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices; no vendor names unless linked to their profile in context; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
